QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_8

question.text: The 'Catch-up' clause in a Category II AIF waterfall specifies that:

answer.text: The manager is allocated residual profits after hurdle is paid, until the manager reaches its pre-determined share of total profits
The manager receives 100% of management fees retrospectively for missed years
Investors catch up on deferred distributions at fund wind-up
GST on management fees is collected in a lump sum at fund termination

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines catch-up as the rate at which residual profits, after return of capital and payment of the hurdle, are allocated to the manager so that the manager 'catches up' to its pre-agreed share of total profits. A 100% catch-up allocates all post-hurdle residual to the manager until the target share is reached. The Trap: Option B is invented. Option C reverses who receives the catch-up. Option D describes an unrelated tax mechanic. Note: The workbook illustrates catch-up with 40% and 100% examples and notes that higher catch-up rates are more manager-favourable and riskier for investors.
